sentences: Financial regulators in Britain have imposed a rather unusual rule on the bosses of big banks.
Starting next year, any guaranteed bonus of top executives could be delayed 10 years if their banks are under investigation for wrongdoing.
The main purpose of this “clawback” rule is to hold bankers accountable for harmful risk-taking and to restore public trust in financial institutions.
Yet officials also hope for a much larger benefit: more long-term decision-making, not only by banks but by all corporations, to build a stronger economy for future generations.
translations: 英国的金融监管机构对大银行的老板们实施了一条相当不寻常的规定。
从明年开始，如果高管所在的银行因不当行为正在接受调查，他们的任何保证奖金都可能被推迟10年发放。
这项“追回”规则的主要目的是让银行家对有害的风险承担行为负责，并恢复公众对金融机构的信任。
然而，官员们还希望获得一个更大的好处：不仅是银行，而是所有公司都能做出更多长期决策，为子孙后代建设更强大的经济。

sentences: “Short-termism,” or the desire for quick profits, has worsened in publicly traded companies, says the Bank of England’s top economist, Andrew Haldane.

He quotes a giant of classical economics, Alfred Marshall, in describing this financial impatience as acting like “children who pick the plums out of their pudding to eat them at once” rather than putting them aside to be eaten last.
translations: 英国央行首席经济学家安德鲁·霍尔丹表示，“短期主义”，即追求快速利润的欲望，在上市公司中已经恶化。
他引用古典经济学巨匠阿尔弗雷德·马歇尔的话，将这种金融上的不耐烦描述为“从布丁里挑出李子立刻吃掉的孩子”，而不是把它们放在一边最后吃。

sentences: The average time for holding a stock in both the United States and Britain, he notes, has dropped from seven years to seven months in recent decades.
Transient investors, who demand high quarterly profits from companies, can hinder a firm’s efforts to invest in long-term research or to build up customer loyalty.
This has been dubbed “quarterly capitalism. ”
translations: 他指出，在美国和英国，持有股票的平均时间在近几十年里已从七年下降到七个月。
要求公司提供高额季度利润的短期投资者，可能会阻碍公司投资于长期研究或建立客户忠诚度的努力。
这被称为“季度资本主义”。

sentences: In addition, new digital technologies have allowed more rapid trading of equities, quicker use of information, and thus shorter attention spans in financial markets.
“There seems to be a predominance of short-term thinking at the expense of long-term investing,” said Commissioner Daniel Gallagher of the US Securities and Exchange Commission in a speech this week.
translations: 此外，新的数字技术使得股票交易更加迅速，信息利用更加快捷，从而导致金融市场的注意力持续时间更短。
美国证券交易委员会委员丹尼尔·加拉格尔本周在一次演讲中表示：“似乎短期思维占主导地位，而牺牲了长期投资。”

sentences: In the US, the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 has pushed most public companies to defer performance bonuses for senior executives by about a year, slightly helping reduce “short-termism. ”
In its latest survey of CEO pay, The Wall Street Journal finds that “a substantial part” of executive pay is now tied to performance.
translations: 在美国，2002年的《萨班斯-奥克斯利法案》已促使大多数上市公司将高管的绩效奖金推迟约一年发放，这略微有助于减少“短期主义”。
《华尔街日报》在最新的CEO薪酬调查中发现，高管薪酬的“很大一部分”现在与业绩挂钩。

sentences: Much more could be done to encourage “long-termism,” such as changes in the tax code and quicker disclosure of stock acquisitions.
In France, shareholders who hold onto a company investment for at least two years can sometimes earn more voting rights in a company.
translations: 为了鼓励“长期主义”，还可以做更多事情，例如修改税法以及加快股票收购的披露。
在法国，持有公司投资至少两年的股东有时可以在公司中获得更多的投票权。

sentences: Within companies, the right compensation design can provide incentives for executives to think beyond their own time at the company and on behalf of all stakeholders.
Britain’s new rule is a reminder to bankers that society has an interest in their performance, not just for the short term but for the long term.
translations: 在公司内部，正确的薪酬设计可以激励高管们超越自己在公司的任期，并代表所有利益相关者进行思考。
英国的新规定提醒银行家们，社会对他们的表现感兴趣，不仅是短期表现，还有长期表现。
